# Briefklar

> Briefklar explains German authority letters (immigration office, tax office, health insurance, broadcasting
> fee) in plain language in German, English, French and Arabic, with the deadline as a calendar file, a checklist
> and a reply draft. OCR and redaction of personal data run on the server before the text reaches the LLM (with a
> preview so the user can check it; detection is not perfect). Letters are kept only for processing and deleted
> immediately afterwards; only user accounts and a daily usage counter are stored. A portfolio project by Omar
> Fourati with public source code. Not legal advice. When in doubt, ask the authority.

- App and demo (read-only demo account with three example letters): https://briefklar.omarfourati.de/app/login
- Source code: https://github.com/omarfourati-dev/Briefklar
- Author: Omar Fourati, Full-Stack Developer – https://omarfourati.de

## How it works
1. Upload a photo or PDF (or paste text). Tesseract (German) and poppler extract the text on the server.
2. Redaction replaces names, addresses, IBAN, tax ID, file numbers, phone numbers, e-mail and birth dates with
   placeholders such as [NAME_1]. The user sees a preview and can redact more words by clicking them.
3. Only the redacted text is sent to OpenAI for the explanation (structured JSON output). The browser puts the
   original values back.

## Technology
- Backend: Go (net/http, pgx, slog, embed), Tesseract, poppler, PostgreSQL (accounts and usage counters only)
- Frontend: Angular (standalone components, signals), Tailwind CSS, right-to-left layout for Arabic
- Quality: Go table tests, testcontainers-go, Angular unit tests, Playwright end-to-end tests in CI
- Operations: Docker, GitHub Actions, Caddy, Prometheus and Grafana with alerts
